question: What is the basic functional unit of the kidney responsible for urine production?
explanation: The nephron is the microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney that filters blood and forms urine. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h1)

question: During which phase of urine formation does the body reclaim essential nutrients back into the bloodstream?
explanation: Tubular reabsorption moves water and vital solutes out of the filtrate and back into the peritubular capillaries. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which type of urine sample is best for detecting pregnancy and concentrated substances?
explanation: The first morning sample is the most concentrated because urine accumulates in the bladder overnight. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why do we use a clean-catch midstream technique for urine cultures?

options.A: It measures the exact volume produced over a set time
options.B: It stops red blood cells from entering the collection cup
options.C: It prevents skin germs from contaminating the bacterial culture
options.D: It ensures the bladder is completely empty before testing

explanation: Washing the urethral area and letting the initial stream flush away external organisms prevents false-positive culture results. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h2)

question: Finding nitrites on a routine urine dipstick test usually points to which condition?
explanation: Certain bacteria reduce urinary nitrates to nitrites, signaling a likely bacterial infection in the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the main reason urine dipsticks must be stored away from moisture and heat?

options.A: To keep the container sterile for patient testing
options.B: To stop the plastic strips from bending out of shape
options.C: To ensure the color chart remains bright and readable
options.D: To prevent chemical damage to the reactive pads

explanation: Exposure to environmental moisture and heat alters the chemical reagents on the pads, leading to false results. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h3)

question: What are the small tube-shaped structures formed in the kidney tubules that can show up in urine sediment?
explanation: Casts are formed when protein precipitates within the renal tubules and takes on the shape of the lumen. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h4)

question: What does finding many white blood cells and white blood cell casts in urine sediment usually mean?

options.B: Contamination of the sample with normal vaginal secretions
options.C: Normal breakdown of blood cells after heavy exercise
options.D: Active inflammation or infection in the urinary tract

explanation: White blood cells and their casts signify an active inflammatory process, often due to a kidney infection or severe bladder infection. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h4)

question: What bacterial count in a urine sample usually confirms a significant urinary tract infection?
explanation: A bacterial count of 10^5 CFU/mL or higher in a clean-catch sample is the standard benchmark for significant bacteriuria. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h5)

question: A patient's urine culture report shows bacterial growth with an antibiotic labeled as 'resistant'. What does this mean for treatment?

options.A: The patient is allergic to that particular pharmaceutical agent
options.B: That specific drug will not successfully kill the infecting bacteria
options.C: The laboratory made an error during testing
options.D: The drug should be given at double the standard dose to work

explanation: A resistant label indicates the pathogen is not inhibited by that antibiotic, meaning the drug should be avoided. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h5)

question: How should you start the collection process for an accurate 24-hour urine test?

options.A: Collect all urine starting immediately with the first morning void
options.B: Save the very first morning urine sample in a separate small container
options.C: Have the patient empty the bladder completely and discard that urine
options.D: Force fluids for two hours before starting the official collection timer

explanation: Discarding the first morning void marks zero time; starting with an empty bladder ensures old urine is not counted in the test. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why are 24-hour urine collections necessary for certain laboratory tests?

options.A: Substance levels change throughout the day, so a total daily measurement is needed
options.B: Bacteria take a full day to grow large enough to view under a microscope
options.C: Single spot samples cannot be processed by automated hospital lab machines
options.D: Kidneys only filter specific proteins during sleep

explanation: Many substances vary in concentration across hours, so a 24-hour pool provides an accurate average daily output. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why does a urine sample left at room temperature for over two hours give unreliable results?

options.A: Bacteria multiply and cells break down, changing the findings
options.B: All glucose molecules evaporate into the air
options.C: Reagents on the test strips stop reacting with fluid
options.D: The plastic collection container begins to dissolve

explanation: Prolonged room temperature delay causes bacterial overgrowth and cellular breakdown, leading to false test values. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h7)

question: How should a nurse instruct a female patient to clean her genital area before a clean-catch urine collection?

options.A: Scrub the area vigorously in a circular motion
options.B: Wash using standard bath soap and rinse with tap water
options.C: Wipe from front to back using antiseptic wipes
options.D: Clean from back to front to reach the lower area

explanation: Wiping from front to back prevents the introduction of germs from the anal area into the urinary opening. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h7)
